provenance: Bounded clean-room comparison of endpoint-product bisection hypotheses against eight previously saved public SEOBNRv4 output rows. The public API output is consumed only as copied arrays and epoch metadata; clean SEOBNRv4 Hamiltonian/flux code evaluates omega. No LAL source or private waveform implementation is inspected.
primary_reference: Bohé et al., Improved effective-one-body model for coalescing nonprecessing binary black holes, arXiv:1611.03703 (equation context).

endpoint_semantics.left: clean omega argmax sample on returned postpeak_state[0]
endpoint_semantics.source: observable returned samples only; no public implementation source inspection
endpoint_semantics.derivative: clean local polynomial derivative on fixed contiguous stencil

bisection_algorithm.update_rule: At each midpoint, if f(left)*f(mid)>0 move left=mid; if f(left)*f(mid)<0 move right=mid; return the interval midpoint. A zero midpoint collapses the interval.
bisection_algorithm.candidate_status: A sign-changing endpoint pair is a valid derivative bracket. Same-sign endpoint candidates are retained as nonbracketing algorithm outputs and are not labeled roots.

gps_quantization.interval_definition: observed epoch +/- 0.5 ns, converted to -epoch initial-origin M coordinate

gps_quantization.interpretation: The interval is the nearest-GPS-nanosecond quantization interval used for a numerical comparison; it does not establish the producer's internal timestamp representation.

interpretation: The next-sample-minus-dt/2048 value is the exact midpoint returned by ten generic updates when both endpoint derivatives have the same sign and the update keeps moving the left endpoint rightward. This is an implementation-convention hypothesis, not an inferred physical time shift. Sign-changing rows are evaluated as ordinary bisection brackets; same-sign rows retain their nonbracketing status.
runtime_recommendation: Do not install an epoch correction from these candidate comparisons. If compatibility with a public epoch becomes a product requirement, supporting an explicit, separately named discrete epoch convention could be considered only after an independent black-box validation; the continuous orbital-frequency event remains the clean runtime origin.
